clue.text: Fred led me, that is understood, into PEPs

indicators.note: into says the phrase for understood goes inside the plural of pep

parts.note: pep, as in liveliness or spirit, is ginger, so PEPs are gingers
Roger is the radio reply meaning the message is received and understood

explanation.surface: A dancer recalls being steered by Fred, the point being taken, into some lively numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire led Ginger Rogers round the dance floor, so the definition is the actress speaking; 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the dancing partner who led the actress in their famous film routines, so she is the dancer he led.

clue.text: Decoration has to take ring off

indicators.note: off, in the sense of gone wrong or out of order, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a ring as a piece of finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'take ring off' but is the anagram signal working on HAS and RING together; 'to take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is a decorative trimming on a dish, an embellishment.

clue.text: Integral part of anagrammatical clue in up-and-coming paper

indicators.note: in places the shuffled clue letters inside the newspaper turned upside down
in a down clue, coming up means the newspaper's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: anagrammatical announces that the next word is to be treated as an anagram

explanation.surface: A rising newspaper is said to have an anagram clue at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-and-coming' turns the newspaper to NUS, and 'anagrammatical' rearranges the next word to UCLE; 'in' then splits NUS after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central, essential core of something, the integral part around which the rest forms.

clue.text: Jump between European clubs at Derby?

parts.note: entre is the French, so European, word for between
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a derby is a bowler hat, the American name for it

explanation.surface: A football fan asks about a leap between European clubs playing a game at Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English football city, but here it is the hat; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in the air.

clue.text: He steps up to sum up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pacer is one who paces, someone or something that steps

explanation.surface: A man climbs some stairs to tot up a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PACER around; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise briefly what has already been said.

clue.text: The Irish law books facing the viewer

parts.note: the Garda is the police force of Ireland, the Irish law
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Irish police are pictured with legal volumes turned towards an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: GARDANT is a heraldic term, also spelt guardant.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an animal shown gardant has its head turned to look out at the person viewing the shield.

clue.text: Win back by working miracle

indicators.note: working, as in being worked or kneaded into shape, asks for the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regains something by performing a miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal on MIRACLE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or win it back after losing it.

clue.text: Thus does sneak preview?

parts.note: a sneak is a sneak thief, who looks over a building in advance of a burglary

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to inspect premises beforehand with a view to robbing them, a burglar's preview.

clue.text: Something to eat and it's time for a fool to go to bed

parts.note: April the first, written APR I, is April Fools' Day
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A jester eats a snack before turning in for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: APR I is the date style for April 1, All Fools' Day, with the Roman numeral for one; 'and it's' and 'to go to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit, something one eats.

clue.text: Capital A consumed by body, not E

indicators.note: consumed by means the A is swallowed inside the other word
not E means that letter is taken out of the word for body

parts.note: carcase is a variant spelling of carcass, a dead body

explanation.surface: A grade A item is eaten by a body, the letter E excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops E from CARCASE to leave CARCAS, and 'consumed by' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

clue.text: Only the boys' marks should be raised!

definitions.text: Only the boys' marks should be raised!

parts.words: Only the boys' marks should be raised!
parts.note: read as a teacher's comment about grades, it is in fact a remark that favours one sex

explanation.definitionFit: Saying only boys deserve higher grades is a comment discriminating against girls, a chauvinist utterance.

clue.text: Drug taken by disgusting old solver — this looks bad

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
vile means disgusting
ye is the old word for you, and you are the solver

explanation.surface: A revolting elderly crossword fan takes drugs, and it doesn't look good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is a link joining E to VILE; 'solver' means you, the person doing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent stare believed to bring harm, literally a bad look.

clue.text: Partisans on hand, or soldiers on foot

definitions.meaning: a body of supporters united in a common cause, here ready and present
an ancient close-packed formation of infantry

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves also hint at the bone sense: a finger bone on the hand and a toe bone on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Phalanx means a tight united group of supporters and a massed infantry formation; it is also a bone of finger or toe.

clue.text: They mark boundaries down

parts.note: these are sunken fences, boundaries set down in a ditch so they do not spoil the view

explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a ditch with a wall in it, a garden boundary placed below ground level.

clue.text: It's difficult to find X-rated mishmash of a book

annotationWithheld.why: It's difficult to find X-rated mishmash of a book (4,5): HARD (X-rated) leaves TIMES unexplained, while 'rated' + 'mish' rearranged gives the letters only by splitting 'mishmash' into fodder and indicator, a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: It's difficult to find X-rated mishmash of a book

clue.text: Watch this — in the box — Shearer foul that hurt!

indicators.note: foul, in the sense of messed up, tells us to scramble the footballer's name

parts.note: ow is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: A football commentator describes a foul on Alan Shearer in the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer was an England striker, and 'the box' looks like the penalty area; a raree show was a peep show viewed in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree show was a travelling peep show carried in a box, which spectators watched through a hole.

clue.text: Frequent traveller using "The Black Dog"

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A regular traveller uses a pub called The Black Dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Black Dog' looks like a pub name; 'using' and 'The' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy person who flies frequently between fashionable places.

clue.text: Being this, he is leaving the land

definitions.text: Being this, he is leaving the land

parts.words: Being this, he is leaving the land
parts.note: he is dying, leaving the country for good, and also bequeathing his land because he made a will

explanation.definitionFit: Someone testate has died having made a valid will, so his estate passes as he directed.

clue.text: Dearest possession that Mary had, after suffering initial reversal?

indicators.note: suffering a reversal at the start means the first two letters swap places

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Mary had a little lamb, and little is wee

explanation.surface: Mary's treasured pet is hinted at after a setback at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering initial reversal' swaps the first two letters, WE becoming EW. The phrase comes from Nathan's parable in the Bible, about a poor man's one beloved lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is an idiom, from the Bible, for one's single most treasured possession.

clue.text: … to come back on 'The Dog"

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, someone returns to a pub called The Dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 16 across and its pub; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, to come back after an interval.

clue.text: Italian cases covering over a violin

indicators.note: covering means the words spread over the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: Italian cases are draped over a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' says the answer runs across the words over a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels from Italy, cases enclosing a filling.

clue.text: Means by which to preserve London Town

definitions.meaning: a process of keeping food by sealing it in tins
an area of east London whose name ends in Town

explanation.walkthrough: Canning Town is a district in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Canning is a food preservation method and Canning Town is part of the London borough of Newham.

clue.text: Look at "P" breaking up the sound of "B"

indicators.note: breaking up means the letter splits the other word apart

parts.note: the letter B is pronounced bee, which is an insect
taken as written

explanation.surface: A phonetics lesson compares the letter P with B.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' puts P inside INSECT, the creature the letter B names when said out.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely, to look at it.

clue.text: Is he up to repairs?

parts.note: a workman who climbs up onto a roof to mend it, capable of the job

explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays and repairs roof tiles, so he goes up for roof repairs.

clue.text: Poison churchman during "Omen" remake

indicators.note: during places the churchman's title inside the reworked film name
remake asks for the film title to be made up again with letters rearranged

parts.note: Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A priest is poisoned while a horror film is being remade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remake' turns OMEN into ENOM, and 'during' puts VEN in the middle. The Omen is a horror film that was remade.
explanation.definitionFit: To envenom is to put poison into something, to poison it.

clue.text: Hang around Virginia, seeking labour

indicators.note: around means the word for hang goes round the state abbreviation

parts.note: to trail is to hang down loosely behind
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone loiters in Virginia looking for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang around' reads as loiter, but 'around' is the container signal; 'seeking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail means hard work or toil, and also the labour of childbirth.

clue.text: Pro receives one more likely to have been supplied by Del Boy

definitions.text: more likely to have been supplied by Del Boy

indicators.note: receives means the professional takes the numeral in

parts.note: pro is slang for a prostitute, a hooker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A professional gets something that a dodgy market trader probably sold.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy is the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; hooky is British slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are hookier are more likely stolen, the kind a shady trader sells cheap.

clue.text: John's sex drive?

parts.note: a john is a prostitute's client, and his drive is a slow car journey looking for one

explanation.definitionFit: The practice is driving slowly along the street to solicit prostitutes, which is what a punter does.
